==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/kuːl ˈdaʊn/}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-cool down.wav|a=Southern England}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb|*}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}}
## To become [[cool]]er; to be reduced in [[temperature]].
##: {{syn|en|cool off}}
##: {{ant|en|warm up|hot up}}
##: {{cot|en|warm down}}
##: {{ux|en|You can drink the coffee when it's '''cooled down'''.}}
## To become less [[agitated]] or [[excited]].
##: {{syn|en|calm down}}
##: {{ux|en|I'd love to go to Israel, but I'll have to wait until the violence '''cools down'''.}}
## To [[decrease]] in [[degree]] or [[intensity]].
##* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=2022-05-17|author=Coral Murphy Marcos|title=Retail sales rise for the fourth straight month as prices keep climbing.|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/05/17/business/retail-sales-april-inflation.html|passage=The increase in spending in the United States last month follows a revised 1.4 percent month-over-month gain in March, when prices for gasoline soared amid Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Gas prices '''cooled down''' slightly in April but were still at elevated levels, while oil prices remain volatile.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250723041219/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/05/17/business/retail-sales-april-inflation.html|archivedate=23 July 2025}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}}
## To cause (something) to become [[cooler]]; to reduce the [[temperature]] of.
##: {{ux|en|We had to '''cool down''' the equipment with water before using it.}}
## To cause (someone) to become less [[agitated]] or [[excited]].
##: {{syn|en|calm down}}
##: {{ux|en|Dave was kicking and screaming, so I had to '''cool''' him '''down''' with some mellow music.}}

====Derived terms====
* {{l|en|cooldown|pos=n}}
